title: Chimichurri
subtitle: Argentinian parsley and garlic sauce for grilled meats
excerpt: A vibrant, herby Argentinian condiment made from parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, and olive oil. The essential accompaniment to any grilled or barbecued steak.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chimichurri is an uncooked herb sauce from Argentina and Uruguay, used both as a marinade and as a condiment for grilled meats. The origin of the name is disputed: one popular theory traces it to the Basque Country (many nineteenth-century immigrants to Argentina were Basque), where tximitxurri means a mixture of several things. The sauce is made in two main versions: the standard green version (chimichurri verde) with parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, and olive oil; and a red version (chimichurri rojo) with the addition of red pepper and paprika. The sauce should rest for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow the flavours to meld: freshly made chimichurri tastes sharp and raw; rested chimichurri tastes rounded and complex. It keeps for up to a week in the fridge.

content.text: The parsley should be finely chopped by hand rather than blended: a blended chimichurri is a puree and loses the characteristic coarse texture. Use a large, sharp knife and chop until the parsley is fine but still has body. The sauce should rest for at least 30 minutes before serving: the vinegar needs time to soften the raw garlic edge and the herbs need time to infuse the oil. Taste after resting and adjust the seasoning.

items.preparation: leaves and fine stems, finely chopped
finely chopped; or a pinch of chilli flakes

content.text: Finely chop the parsley by hand. Combine with all the other ingredients in a bowl or jar and stir thoroughly. The sauce will look quite liquid and separated at this stage: stir just before serving.
Leave to rest for at least 30 minutes at room temperature before serving. Taste and adjust the vinegar, salt, and chilli. Serve alongside grilled steak, lamb cutlets, or roasted vegetables.
